extracted.intended_audience: parties and counsel in PTAB inter partes review proceedings (petitioners and patent owners); patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the factors the Patent Trial and Appeal Board considers in exercising its discretion to deny institution under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) where there is a parallel district court (or ITC) proceeding. The order authorizes supplemental briefing and explains how to present facts and evidence relevant to those factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence or likelihood of a district court stay
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the court granted a stay or evidence exists that one may be granted if a proceeding is instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A district court stay pending resolution of the PTAB trial allays concerns about inefficiency and duplication and has strongly weighed against exercising authority to deny institution under NHK. If the district court denied a stay but indicated willingness to reconsider or to consider a renewed motion if PTAB institutes, that guidance (if made of record) also weighs against denial. Conversely, if the court has denied a motion to stay and has not indicated it will reconsider, that fact may weigh in favor of denial. Parties should indicate whether a parallel district court case is stayed or whether a stay is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity of the court's trial date to the Board's projected statutory deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: How close in time the district court trial date is to the Board’s projected statutory deadline for issuing a final written decision (considering the one-year default and potential six-month extension under 35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the court’s trial date is earlier than the projected PTAB final decision deadline, the Board generally weighs this in favor of denying institution. If the trial date is at/around or after the Board’s projected deadline, other factors will carry more weight. Precedent (NHK) applies where district court trial is scheduled to finish before the Board’s final decision date; by contrast, when the trial is scheduled after the PTAB deadline, the Board may be less likely to deny based on timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in the parallel proceeding by the court and the parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount and type of work already completed in the parallel litigation by the court and parties at the time of the institution decision (e.g., claim construction, substantive orders, discovery and summary judgment activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant investment (e.g., claim construction orders, dispositive motions, closed discovery, jury pretrial readiness) favors denial because it suggests the parallel proceeding is advanced and instituting would lead to duplicative costs and wasted judicial resources. If little or no work has been done in the district court, this factor weighs against denying institution. The weight of claim construction orders may vary by district-court practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap between issues in the petition and the parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which the petition raises the same or substantially the same claims, grounds, arguments, and evidence as those presented in the parallel proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantial overlap (identical claims, grounds, arguments, and evidence) favors denial due to inefficiency and risk of conflicting decisions. If the petition raises materially different grounds or evidence, that tends to weigh against denial. Partial overlap is fact-dependent: challenges to additional claims beyond those in district court may still be inefficient if the overlapping claims are likely to resolve the key issues. Parties should indicate which challenged claims overlap with the district-court case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether the petitioner is the same party as the defendant in the parallel proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner in the PTAB proceeding is the same party (or related) to the defendant in the district court litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner is unrelated to the defendant in the earlier court proceeding, the Board has often weighed that fact against denying institution under NHK. Nonetheless, even an unrelated petitioner may not avoid denial if the issues are the same or substantially similar and other circumstances weigh against duplicative proceedings. Unrelated petitioners should explain other district-court or Federal Circuit proceedings involving the patent to show why addressing similar issues would not be duplicative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merits and other circumstances (holistic assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other circumstances that impact the Board’s exercise of discretion, including the preliminary strength or weakness of the petition’s merits and other non-parallel factors (e.g., serial petitions, parallel petitions, § 325(d) issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board takes a balanced, holistic view of all relevant circumstances, including the merits. Particularly strong merits on the preliminary record can favor institution even if other factors point toward denial, because instituting preserves the PTAB option should the parallel proceeding settle or fail to resolve patentability. Weak merits weigh toward denial when combined with other denial factors. The Board need not conduct a full merits analysis but will consider apparent strengths/weaknesses. Parties should explain serial-petition issues, multiple parallel petitions, or § 325(d) concerns and their effect on system efficiency and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition timing and petitioner diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the petitioner filed its IPR petition expeditiously after becoming aware of the asserted claims and within the one-year window of 35 U.S.C. § 315(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner filed promptly (e.g., shortly after learning which claims were asserted), that fact weighs against denying institution. If the petitioner delayed filing despite being aware of the parallel litigation (or cannot explain delay), that favors denial because it may impose unfair costs on the patent owner. The Board recognizes reasons to wait (e.g., to see which claims are asserted) but will weigh the timing facts presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: ITC proceedings and stays under 28 U.S.C. § 1659
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there is a parallel ITC investigation that has stayed a district-court proceeding under 28 U.S.C. § 1659 and whether the ITC will decide the same or substantially similar issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District-court stays under § 1659 often arise during parallel ITC investigations. An earlier ITC trial date may favor denial if the ITC will decide substantially similar patentability issues. Parties should state whether the PTAB disputes before the ITC will resolve all or substantially all patentability disputes. Note: ITC final invalidity determinations do not have preclusive effect, but they are practically difficult to disregard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence on the record and permissible supplemental filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties are authorized to submit supplemental briefing addressing facts relevant to the NHK factors, and such briefing may be accompanied by documentary evidence but not by declaratory evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Order authorizes a limited supplemental exchange: Petitioner may file a reply (no more than 10 pages) limited to discretionary denial under § 314(a); Patent Owner may file a sur-reply (no more than 10 pages) limited to that issue. Documentary evidence may accompany filings to support factual assertions, but declaratory (e.g., witness declarations) evidence is not permitted with the supplemental briefs. Parties should present facts relevant to the enumerated factors and any other circumstances impacting discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: System efficiency, fairness, and patent quality as guiding principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board weighs considerations of system efficiency, fairness to the parties, and the integrity/quality of the patent system when exercising discretion to deny or institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factors are considered to determine whether efficiency and integrity of the system are best served by denying or instituting review. Examples cited include avoiding duplication of work by two tribunals, preventing unnecessary litigation costs, and protecting the parties’ and court’s invested resources. The Board takes a holistic approach and balances these policy considerations with the merits and factual circumstances of each case.
